nodes.name: Lead Webhook
nodes.notes: Entry point. This is what a real form/CRM webhook would POST to instead of data/synthetic_leads.py. responseMode is 'responseNode' rather than n8n's default 'immediately' - that's what lets the 'Respond to Webhook' node further down send back the agent's actual qualification result instead of an empty 200.

nodes.name: Qualify Lead (agent service)
nodes.notes: Calls the FastAPI agent service (agent/main.py's POST /qualify) and gets back the full qualification decision. host.docker.internal is how a container reaches a service running on the host machine - swap it for a real hostname once this deploys alongside the client's actual stack, and note that if AGENT_API_KEY is set on the agent service (see agent/security.py), this node also needs an X-API-Key header added under Options > Headers with the matching value - deliberately not hardcoded here so a real secret never ends up committed in this file.

nodes.name: Respond to Webhook
nodes.notes: Sends the agent's qualification result straight back to whatever called the webhook - runs in parallel with 'Route by Tier' below, off the same 'Qualify Lead' output, so the caller doesn't have to wait for the notification branch to finish.

nodes.name: Route by Tier
nodes.notes: Checked top to bottom, first match wins. Rule 1 stops repeats: a lead the agent has already decided (duplicate=true) was routed the first time, so it goes nowhere. Rule 2 sends anything the agent flagged needs_review (confidence under business.yaml's review.min_confidence) to the review channel, whatever its tier. The other four route on the agent's `tier` field (hot/warm/cold/spam - see agent/schema.py's Tier type), one output per match. Each output wire below goes to its own placeholder Set node - swap those for the client's real Slack/CRM/marketing-automation nodes.

nodes.name: Slack: #hot-leads
nodes.notes: REAL, not a placeholder - posts to whatever Slack Incoming Webhook URL is set as SLACK_WEBHOOK_HOT (see .env.example / docker-compose.yml). Create one in under 2 minutes at https://api.slack.com/apps > your app > Incoming Webhooks. Until that env var is set, this node will fail visibly in n8n's execution log rather than silently doing nothing - that's the signal setup isn't finished yet.

nodes.name: Duplicate: already routed

assignments.name: notification
assignments.value: =No action - this exact lead (same email + message) was already qualified and routed as lead #{{ $json.id }}.

nodes.notes: Idempotency: the agent returned its stored decision instead of re-scoring, so nothing is posted again.

nodes.name: Slack: #lead-review
nodes.notes: The human-review path. Low-confidence leads land here instead of being auto-routed by tier. Posts to SLACK_WEBHOOK_REVIEW - point it at a channel the team actually triages.

nodes.name: Slack: #sales-smb
nodes.notes: REAL - same pattern as the hot-lead node, posting to a separate SLACK_WEBHOOK_WARM URL (can be the same channel or a different one - your call). Swap for a real CRM-write node instead if the client's SMB pipeline lives in a CRM rather than Slack.

nodes.name: Notify: nurture sequence (placeholder)

assignments.name: notification
assignments.value: =Replace this Set node with a real marketing-automation trigger: enroll {{ $json.email }} in the nurture sequence.

nodes.notes: PLACEHOLDER - swap for a real marketing-automation enrollment call (Mailchimp, HubSpot, etc.).

nodes.name: Discard: log only

assignments.name: notification
assignments.value: =No action - logged in the agent's audit trail via /qualify. Nothing sent downstream.

nodes.notes: Deliberately a dead end, not a placeholder to fill in - spam is already fully handled by the agent's own audit trail (agent/store.py). Nothing needs to happen here.

nodes.name: Escape for Slack
nodes.notes: Security fix from the agent-red-team scan (SECURITY_FINDINGS.md): nothing a sender typed, or the model quoted, can become a live Slack @channel ping or link.
